A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same partitioning-classification work and provide readable mathematical content throughout. V3's Section 5 proofs correspond to v4's Appendix A; no material gaps prevent comparison.

before.justification: V3 reports mathematical convergence bounds, analytical examples and proofs, but no experimental, simulation or empirical data-analysis outcomes.

after.justification: V4 remains theoretical, including Appendix A. Its additional lemmas and analytical examples do not constitute original empirical results.

M1.justification: The cell-count estimators, binary sign and multiclass argmax classifiers, and Laplace privacy mechanism remain unchanged. Revised guarantees and additional bandwidth guidance do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets for training or evaluation. Binary/multiclass and observable/private classification remain the theoretical settings; new healthcare and finance examples are motivation, not evaluated domains.

E2.justification: Both versions compare analytical guarantees with prior theoretical bounds, without experimentally evaluating comparator methods. No evaluated baseline set changes.

E3.justification: Neither version reports experimental splits, training budgets or testing protocols. Changes to theoretical bandwidth prescriptions are not changes to an evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: Neither version contains empirical ablations, robustness tests or error studies. Revisions to the constructed density examples and mathematical error bounds belong to the theoretical analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The CLT and Berry–Esséen arguments concern theoretical approximation errors, not empirical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Neither PDF contains measured performance results or empirical result entries. Revised asymptotic guarantees and analytical example parameters are assessed under T1.

T1.justification: V4 adds Lemmas 3.1–3.2 and their proofs relating the margin/density conditions. It corrects v3's local-density lemma to guarantee exponents up to min(gamma,1), adds the missing expectation to the main nonprivate bound, and changes the privacy remainder from O(sigma_Z/(n h^d)) to O(sigma_Z/(n h^d_a)). The private-rate discussion removes the d <= 2d_a restriction and revises its exponent. These substantively alter mathematical statements and their justification.

C1.justification: The abstract replaces the claim of an exact convergence rate with a bound that can attain minimax rates, while Section 2 drops the general estimation-error lower-bound assertion. The central contributions for observable/private and binary/multiclass classification remain.

C2.justification: V4 adds explanations of bounded-support and tail restrictions, the CLT limitation on super-fast rates, quadratic class-count dependence and conditions for matching minimax rates. It also corrects Example 2's interpretation by acknowledging that SDA holds for -1 < delta <= 0.

D1.justification: Section 3 newly describes O(n) nonprivate aggregation, O(h^(-d_a)) occupied-cell storage and O(n h^(-d_a)) private workload, and supplies multiclass bandwidth guidance. These are analytical implementation details; no code, hardware or measured runtime information is added.

R1.justification: The same 22 works are cited. V4 adds an explicit claim after Theorem 2.3 that this is the first multiclass plug-in convergence result without SDA using only margin-type conditions, and sharpens comparisons with existing minimax guarantees.

P1.justification: V4 substantially revises and expands the main exposition, standardizes multi-class terminology, and adds proof summaries and assumption explanations. Proofs move from Section 5 to Appendix A, references precede the appendix, and the local-density lemma moves before the main nonprivate theorem.

P2.justification: The document is comprehensively reformatted, with different page dimensions, typography, text width, title/author arrangement, headers and equation wrapping. Neither version contains figures or tables.

improvement.justification: V4 improves precision by correcting the expected-risk statement and local-density lemma, aligning claims with upper-bound proofs, and explaining assumptions and limitations. These gains are qualified by new inconsistencies: the bandwidth recommendation after Theorem 3.4 uses 1/(2+d_a), conflicting with the displayed privacy bound and earlier 1/(2+2d_a) prescription, and the new Example 3 discussion uses an undefined delta. The overall improvement is therefore limited.
